idea.name: Cheesy Chicken, Broccoli & Rice Bake
idea.description: Golden-seared chicken thighs on garlicky broth-baked rice and tender broccoli, finished under a bubbling blanket of sharp cheddar.
idea.pairingNote: Chicken, broccoli, rice and cheddar is a classic comfort casserole, and the lemon zest keeps it bright.

written.name: Cheesy Chicken, Broccoli & Rice Bake
written.description: Golden-seared chicken thighs on garlicky broth-baked rice and tender broccoli, finished under a bubbling blanket of sharp cheddar.

ingredients.name: Chicken, broilers or fryers, dark meat, thigh, meat only, raw
ingredients.label: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: trimmed, cut into large bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, enriched
ingredients.label: long-grain white rice

ingredients.name: Soup, chicken broth, low sodium, canned
ingredients.label: low-sodium chicken broth

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and set out a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Season {1} chicken with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and dried thyme.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden, then move it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add {6} onion with a pinch of salt, and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in 3 minced garlic cloves and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add {3} rice and stir for 1 minute to coat it in the pan juices, then pour in {5} broth and bring to a simmer.
Pour the rice and broth into the baking dish, spread it evenly, and set the chicken on top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover, tuck {2} broccoli into the rice around the chicken, cover again, and bake for 12–15 minutes more until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Scatter {4} cheddar over the top and bake uncovered for 5 minutes until melted and bubbling.
Grate lemon zest over the top, rest for 5 minutes, and serve.
written.tip: Toast the dried thyme and smoked paprika in the hot skillet for a few seconds before the broth goes in to bring out a deeper, smoky flavor.
